title: the_parking_spot
beats: My HOA fined me two hundred dollars for parking in front of my own house.
Not blocking a hydrant. Not blocking a driveway. My car. My curb. Two hundred dollars.
The fine notice was signed personally by the HOA president. With a smiley face.
So I did what any petty, law-abiding homeowner would do. I read the bylaws.
All ninety-four pages. Twice. With a highlighter.
Turns out the parking fine was technically legit. Page thirty-eight.
But buried on page seventy-one, I found something better.
Decorative lawn structures require written board approval. Fifty dollars per structure. Per day.
The HOA president's front yard? Thirty-one garden gnomes. Zero approvals on file. I checked the meeting minutes going back six years.
I filed thirty-one separate complaints on a Monday morning. With photos. And page citations.
By Wednesday, the board had to formally fine its own president. The bylaws gave them no choice. I quoted the mandatory enforcement clause in every single filing.
By Friday, the board owed itself more money than it had collected all year.
The parking rule got repealed at the next meeting. Unanimous vote. It took four minutes.
The gnomes, tragically, did not survive the paperwork. And my curb has never been quieter.
